item.title: Aravind Srinivas：SF 2049 is bigger now, and it's multiplayer. Computer added:
item.description:
SF 2049 is bigger now, and it's multiplayer. Computer added:

Race rooms on Cloudflare Durable Objects. Create a room, share a six-letter code, meet on the Embarcadero grid, race through gate halos with server-side lap timing. Rooms close themselves when empty.

10 new player cars generated with image-to-3D, a studio garage to pick them, and a Blade Runner-style Spinner that flies.
Rapier vehicle physics with handbrake powerslides, a fullscreen city map, time trials, collision sounds, and a rebaked map loyal to the real SF street layout.

The trailer was shot by three agents in parallel: fixed-step 1080p60 capture, a real two-player race on a second GPU, and sound rebuilt from the game's own engine loops. Everything in it is captured gameplay.

https://t.co/VgXOUGpsHF

item.title: Aravind Srinivas：Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done…
item.description:
Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI.

In self-distillation, the same model performs the role of both a teacher and a student. The teacher gets extra information that the student doesn't, and the student learns from feedback provided by the teacher. However, the teacher could still use shortcuts in ways the student has no way to follow.

Our proposed approach, JOLT, trains the teacher as well, to learn from rewards on its own attempts, while penalizing any drift that's far off from what the student model would do. JOLT+ further supplements JOLT by providing the student model outcome-based rewards in addition to the teacher supervision signals.

On the MATH benchmark, we found that JOLT matches GRPO with 6.5x fewer training tokens, while JOLT+ convincingly beats GRPO across math, coding, terminal tasks, and tool use benchmarks.

item.title: Aravind Srinivas：Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with …
item.description:
Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with Perplexity Computer. This user's mechanical keyboard app was Windows only, with no Linux support and no documentation. Computer downloaded the binary in its cloud sandbox, decompiled it with headless Ghidra, and ported it to a native Rust app for Linux.

Computer read the decompiled code to learn how the app drives the keyboard, then rebuilt it piece by piece, complete with keyboard lighting that syncs to music over PipeWire, a 3D view, key remapping, macros and profiles.

https://t.co/eDZwppdI6c

item.title: Aravind Srinivas：We got Computer playing StarCraft against Computer, in real time. No paus…
item.description:
We got Computer playing StarCraft against Computer, in real time. No pausing. The game keeps running while each agent thinks.

Blue 2 – Red 5

Final match. Blue builds up safely, reaches 41 Dragoons, and moves out. Red is waiting with High Templar and hits the army with Psionic Storm. Blue hadn’t scouted what Red was building.

Computer assembled the whole setup: an OpenBW-based Brood War runtime on a VPS, a C++ bridge, and four gameplay tools per agent. Each agent receives its own fog-of-war-limited game state. Recording and camera control run separately; the agents aren’t given video input.

item.title: AravSrinivas：a few open source contributions from perplexity recently:
item.description:
a few open source contributions from perplexity recently:

•pplx-decider-v1-27b: SoTA multimodal decision model. 85.7% average across 11 benchmarks, ahead of Jev.
•pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview: SoTA contextual embeddings, best on ConTEB and turbopuffer context-bench.
•Lily: local inference engine for Apple silicon. rust plus custom metal kernels, no pytorch or mlx. 1.23x faster prefill and 1.35x faster decode than MLX-LM on an M5 Max
•PII-Tracer: 0.6B on-device PII classifier that decides when a hybrid compute task stays on your Mac. beats OpenAI’s Privacy Filter on all 5 public benchmarks. also released with the PII-TRACE benchmark: 13k conversations in 13 languages
•WANDR: benchmark for wide and deep research agents. 500 tasks needing 170k source-backed records
•Numbat: agent detection and response for laptops and workstations. 52 rules, single go binary for macOS, linux and windows
•Bumblebee: read-only supply chain scanner for dev machines. covers packages, MCP configs, and editor and browser extensions.

a lot more open source contributions coming soon!

item.title: AravSrinivas：We’re adding Profiles, Skills, and managed connectors to the Perplexity Agent…
item.description:
We’re adding Profiles, Skills, and managed connectors to the Perplexity Agent API.

A Profile is basically a saved agent where you configure model, instructions, tools, connectors, run settings, all under one versioned ID. A project admin sets it up once and every developer on the project can call it from their own app with the project API key. This helps you avoid copying the same config into every application and updating it in five places when the procedure changes.

Skills are versioned so you can ship v2 of a procedure without touching each integration.

Connectors (GitHub, Slack, Drive, Datadog, Linear, Notion to start) are configured once by the admin. That way, apps don’t hold their own credentials.

Profiles and Skills are live today. Connectors in preview.

https://t.co/deOSF89btK

item.title: AravSrinivas：Our security team spent the last month trying to break SPACE, the sandbox pla…
item.description:
Our security team spent the last month trying to break SPACE, the sandbox platform that runs all of Perplexity Computer. We gave 9 models (Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.1 Pro, etc.) root access inside the VM; in some runs, the full sandbox source code too. We asked them to either escape to the host or reach a URL our network policy blocks.

None of them got out of the VM in 108 runs.

But once we allowed a bit of network access (just PyPI and Ubuntu mirrors so that they could install packages), 4 models managed to reach the blocked URL by:

1. Spoofing DNS responses to our gateway and using the fact that https://t.co/UtoIWyj1yj sits on a Fastly IP shared with thousands of other sites.
2. GPT-5.6 Cyber went through Taboola's image fetcher to a screenshot service and then OCR'd the flag out of the image.

We fixed both issues and made sure the reruns held. We also tested 10 other sandbox providers, and 8 of them had the same IP-sharing problem, eg E2B, Vercel, Modal.

Openly sharing the red teaming research is the best way to build guardrails as an industry, and we look forward to working together with @nvidia to incorporate the guardrails into their Open Agent Safety Platform announced today.

https://t.co/AJ97iFK3XS
